audit_findings.title: Post-anchor refinancing may leave substantial future interest unmodeled
audit_findings.magnitude: Q2 2026 term-loan interest expense was $54.7 million; annualized $218.8 million, versus $93.2 million in FY2025, a computed $125.6 million pre-tax increase equal to 24.9% of $504.1 million anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Higher recurring interest reduces the equity-level OE numerator in every forecast year and terminal value; the debt principal is not deducted in the bridge under this method.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect to pay the 2026 Notes using proceeds from the loans prior to or at maturity in 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated post-anchor change, not merely a refinancing possibility. By June 2026, $2,674.8 million of term loans were outstanding and the 2026 Notes had been repaid. Because FY2025 OE retained substantially lower interest expense, using it unchanged can materially overstate sustainable OE and all scenario values.
audit_findings.action: Rebase OE using the $2,674.8 million June debt balance, actual SOFR-plus-3.75% terms, issuance-cost amortization and a normalized full-year cash-interest rate; apply the appropriate cash-tax effect and rerun every scenario without deducting ordinary principal.

audit_findings.title: Finance-leased infrastructure may evade the maintenance-capex deduction
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 finance-lease asset additions were $147.3 million and principal payments were $128.6 million, versus $21.0 million cash capex and $504.1 million anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: If depreciation was added back while the maintenance-capex deduction captured only cash purchases, required finance-leased infrastructure was omitted from OE.
audit_findings.evidence: For the year ended December 31, 2025, net cash used in financing activities was $1,530.7 million, which primarily consisted of $1,713.9 million for the repurchase of our common stock, $151.0 million for the satisfaction of tax withholding obligations for the release of restricted stock units and awards, $128.6 million in principal payments on finance lease obligations, $11.6 million in principal payments against the term loan facility, and $21.6 million in payments of debt issuance costs and loan commitment fees under the term loan facility.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate that finance leases are a recurring, economically significant source of infrastructure, but the supplied record does not show the maintenance-capex schedule used to calculate OE or establish how much of the leased equipment was maintenance rather than growth investment. The possible omission is large, but the actual adjustment remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Produce the annual OE reconciliation and asset-level maintenance-capex schedule; identify finance-lease additions by refresh, replacement and growth purpose, confirm whether they were already deducted, and rerun OE using one non-duplicative maintenance charge.

audit_findings.title: The dilution ceiling gross-stacks instruments whose payoffs offset
audit_findings.magnitude: 39.7 million gross shares from the 19.6 million 2028 conversion notional and 20.1 million 2028 warrant notional, equal to 12.7% of the 312.609285 million denominator; excludes the separate 18.1 million expired-warrant issue
audit_findings.mechanism: An overstated fully diluted denominator depresses value per share; the note hedge offsets the 2028 conversion spread up to the $46.36 warrant strike, and the warrant contributes dilution only above that strike.
audit_findings.evidence: Taken together, the purchase of the Note Hedges and the sale of the Warrants are intended to offset potential dilution from the conversion of the 2026 Notes and the 2028 Notes and/or reduce any cash payments the Company is required to make in excess of the principal amount of such converted Notes, as the case may be, and to effectively increase the overall conversion price from $ 38.25 per share to $ 46.36 per share and from $ 35.35 per share to $ 46.36 for the 2026 Notes and the 2028 Notes, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The gross stacking is demonstrated by the denominator construction and filed contract terms. The instruments are not simultaneous full-notional common claims. The supplied bear, base and bull values per share are below the $35.35 note conversion price and $46.36 warrant strike, making the ceiling particularly disconnected from scenario economics. Exact net shares remain contract- and settlement-dependent, but 39.7 million gross shares are large enough to affect the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Calculate net incremental shares separately for each scenario using the 2028 note conversion formula, $35.35 hedge strike, $46.36 warrant strike, averaging periods, cash-versus-stock elections and counterparty performance; then rerun per-share values.

audit_findings.title: Expired 2026 warrants remain in the valuation-date denominator
audit_findings.magnitude: Maximum removal of 18.1 million shares, or 5.8% of the denominator; computed values would be $24.15 bear, $27.83 base and $32.16 bull, with a $19.48 base buy-below
audit_findings.mechanism: Removing a stale warrant claim reduces the share denominator and raises value per share.
audit_findings.evidence: Subject to the other terms of the Warrants, the first expiration date applicable to the 2026 Warrants and to the 2028 Warrants is June 1, 2026, and June 1, 2028, respectively, and the final expiration date applicable to the 2026 Warrants and 2028 Warrants is August 10, 2026 and August 10, 2028, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The September 5 valuation date is after the August 10 final expiration, so retaining the warrant notional creates a demonstrated date mismatch unless settlement shares were issued outside the August 3 outstanding count. Even assuming the full 18.1 million shares are removed, the bull value rises only from $30.29 to about $32.16 and remains below the $34.83 market price; the isolated finding therefore does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the final warrant settlement statement and first post-August 10 outstanding-share count; replace the 18.1 million notional with only settlement shares actually issued and confirm the computed per-share rerun.

audit_findings.title: Positive growth may require restoring costs removed from the anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Incremental R&D, infrastructure and customer-acquisition spending would reduce forecast OE and could invalidate the assumed 3%–6% growth path.
audit_findings.evidence: Our new product initiatives, including any AI-based initiatives, are intended to result in growth, but such initiatives require a period of investment and ultimately may not succeed on the timelines we expect or at all.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a forward-looking consistency risk rather than a demonstrated omission. FY2025 R&D fell $182.9 million and sales and marketing fell $90.8 million while revenue declined $27.2 million, but the record does not establish the spending required to deliver future growth. H1 2026 revenue grew only 0.8% while R&D increased 2.6%, showing that the cost-growth relationship is evolving and should be monitored.
audit_findings.action: Build scenario-specific revenue and expense forecasts tying 3% and 6% growth to incremental R&D, hosting, infrastructure and marketing costs; rerun OE using the resulting margins and compare against a zero-growth case.

audit_findings.title: A disclosed future headquarters build-out is not visibly reserved
audit_findings.mechanism: The one-time build-out either reduces excess cash in the equity bridge or increases forecast capital spending and reduces OE.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect to continue purchasing infrastructure equipment to support our user base and expect a one-time incremental investment related to the build-out of our new San Francisco, California headquarters given we will vacate our current San Francisco, California headquarters due to recent sublease activity.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing confirms a planned 2026 build-out, but supplies no remaining commitment or expected total cost. It is therefore a forward-looking cash requirement rather than a presently quantified valuation error. Materiality cannot be established from the $4.5 million of total H1 2026 cash capex because that amount does not identify the remaining headquarters expenditure.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the approved build-out budget, amounts spent through September 5, unpaid invoices, contractual commitments and landlord allowances; deduct the unfunded remainder from bridge cash or include it once in projected capital spending, without double counting.
